History and Approaches: Psychology
The scientific study of behavior and mental processes
Structuralism
Early approach analyzing consciousness into basic elements
Functionalism
Approach studying how mental processes help organisms adapt
Psychoanalytic perspective
Freud's view emphasizing unconscious conflicts and early experience
Behavioral perspective
View that psychology should study observable behavior only
Humanistic perspective
View emphasizing free will, growth, and self-actualization
Cognitive perspective
View focusing on how people think, remember, and process information
Biological perspective
View explaining behavior through genetics, brain, and neurochemistry
Sociocultural perspective
View emphasizing how culture and social context shape behavior
Nature versus nurture
Debate over the relative influence of genes and environment
Research Methods: The outcome variable that is measured
Placing participants into groups by chance to reduce confounds
An uncontrolled factor that could explain the results
Improvement caused by expectation rather than treatment
Design where neither participants nor researchers know group assignment
A statistical relationship between two variables, not proof of causation
Watching behavior in its normal setting without intervention
In-depth investigation of one individual or small group
Ethical requirement that participants agree knowing what is involved
Explaining the study's true purpose to participants afterward
The full group of interest versus the subset actually studied
Biological Bases of Behavior: A nerve cell that transmits electrical and chemical signals
The gap between neurons where neurotransmitters cross
A chemical messenger carrying signals between neurons
Neurotransmitter involved in reward, motivation, and movement
Neurotransmitter affecting mood, sleep, and appetite
Nerves connecting the CNS to the rest of the body
Division that triggers the fight-or-flight response
Division that calms the body and conserves energy
Outer brain layer responsible for complex thought and processing
Brain region handling planning, judgment, and personality
Structure essential for forming new long-term memories
Structure processing fear and emotional responses
The brain's ability to reorganize and form new connections
Sensation and Perception: Sensation
Detecting physical energy from the environment through receptors
Perception
Organizing and interpreting sensory information into meaning
Absolute threshold
The minimum stimulation needed to detect a stimulus half the time
Difference threshold
The smallest detectable difference between two stimuli
Sensory adaptation
Reduced sensitivity after constant exposure to a stimulus
Transduction
Converting physical energy into neural signals
Retina
Light-sensitive inner eye surface containing rods and cones
Rods and cones
Retinal receptors for dim light and for color and detail
Top-down processing
Perception guided by expectation and prior experience
Bottom-up processing
Perception built directly from raw sensory input
Gestalt principles
Rules describing how we group elements into whole forms
Depth perception
Ability to judge distance using binocular and monocular cues
States of Consciousness: Consciousness
Awareness of ourselves and our environment
Circadian rhythm
The roughly 24-hour biological cycle regulating sleep and waking
REM sleep
Sleep stage with rapid eye movement, vivid dreaming, and muscle paralysis
Insomnia
Persistent difficulty falling or staying asleep
Sleep apnea
Disorder involving repeated breathing stoppages during sleep
Narcolepsy
Disorder causing sudden uncontrollable sleep attacks
Hypnosis
A state of heightened suggestibility and focused attention
Depressants
Drugs that slow neural activity, such as alcohol
Stimulants
Drugs that speed neural activity, such as caffeine and amphetamines
Tolerance
Needing larger doses of a drug to feel the same effect
Learning: Classical conditioning
Learning to associate two stimuli, as in Pavlov's dogs
Unconditioned stimulus
A stimulus that naturally triggers a response without learning
Conditioned stimulus
A neutral stimulus that comes to trigger a response after pairing
Operant conditioning
Learning where behavior is shaped by consequences
Positive reinforcement
Adding a desirable stimulus to increase a behavior
Negative reinforcement
Removing an unpleasant stimulus to increase a behavior
Punishment
A consequence that decreases the behavior it follows
Extinction
The fading of a conditioned response when reinforcement stops
Shaping
Reinforcing successive approximations toward a target behavior
Observational learning
Learning by watching and imitating others
Schedule of reinforcement
The pattern determining how often a behavior is rewarded
Latent learning
Learning that occurs without reinforcement and appears only when needed
Memory: Getting information into the memory system
Getting information back out of memory
Brief initial recording of sensory information
Limited-capacity memory held briefly, roughly seven items
Relatively permanent and limitless memory storage
Active processing of incoming and stored information
Grouping items into meaningful units to expand capacity
Conscious repetition of information to retain it
Better long-term retention from distributed rather than massed practice
Older memories disrupting recall of newer information
New learning disrupting recall of older information
Better recall of the first and last items in a list
Memory distortion caused by misleading post-event information
Cognition and Language: Cognition
The mental activities of thinking, knowing, and remembering
Concept
A mental grouping of similar objects, events, or people
Prototype
The best example of a category used for quick comparison
Algorithm
A step-by-step procedure guaranteeing a correct solution
Heuristic
A mental shortcut that is fast but sometimes wrong
Confirmation bias
Tendency to seek evidence supporting existing beliefs
Availability heuristic
Judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind
Representativeness heuristic
Judging by resemblance to a prototype, ignoring base rates
Functional fixedness
Inability to see an object used in an unusual way
Framing
How wording a question influences the decision made
Phoneme
The smallest distinctive sound unit in a language
Morpheme
The smallest unit of language carrying meaning
Motivation and Emotion: Motivation
A need or desire that energizes and directs behavior
Drive-reduction theory
Idea that physiological needs create drives pushing us to reduce them
Maslow's hierarchy of needs
Pyramid ordering needs from physiological to self-actualization
Intrinsic motivation
Doing something for its own inherent satisfaction
Extrinsic motivation
Doing something for external rewards or to avoid punishment
Homeostasis
Maintaining a stable internal physiological state
James-Lange theory
Emotion results from awareness of physiological arousal
Cannon-Bard theory
Arousal and emotional experience occur simultaneously
Schachter-Singer theory
Emotion requires both arousal and a cognitive label
Yerkes-Dodson law
Performance peaks at moderate arousal levels
Developmental Psychology: Developmental psychology
Study of physical, cognitive, and social change across the lifespan
Schema
A mental framework organizing and interpreting information
Assimilation
Fitting new experiences into existing schemas
Accommodation
Adjusting schemas to fit new information
Object permanence
Understanding that objects continue to exist when out of sight
Conservation
Understanding that quantity stays the same despite changes in shape
Attachment
The emotional bond between an infant and caregiver
Secure attachment
Bond where a child explores freely and is comforted by the caregiver's return
Authoritative parenting
Style combining warmth with clear, reasoned limits
Adolescence
The transition period from puberty to independent adulthood
Identity versus role confusion
Erikson's adolescent stage of forming a coherent sense of self
Zone of proximal development
The range between what a learner can do alone and with help
Personality: Personality
An individual's characteristic pattern of thinking, feeling, and acting
Id
Freud's unconscious reservoir of basic drives seeking immediate gratification
Ego
Freud's reality-oriented component mediating between id and superego
Superego
Freud's internalized moral standards and ideals
Defense mechanism
Unconscious strategy reducing anxiety by distorting reality
Repression
Defense mechanism banishing threatening thoughts from awareness
Big Five traits
Openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, and neuroticism
Self-actualization
Reaching one's full potential, the top of Maslow's hierarchy
Unconditional positive regard
Rogers' concept of total acceptance supporting growth
Self-efficacy
Belief in one's ability to succeed at a specific task
Locus of control
The degree to which people believe they control their own outcomes
Reciprocal determinism
Bandura's view that behavior, environment, and cognition interact
Psychological Disorders and Treatment: Abnormal behavior
Behavior that is deviant, distressing, and dysfunctional
DSM
The manual classifying and describing psychological disorders
Generalized anxiety disorder
Persistent, uncontrollable worry not tied to a specific threat
Panic disorder
Recurrent unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms
Phobia
Persistent irrational fear of a specific object or situation
Obsessive-compulsive disorder
Intrusive thoughts paired with repetitive ritual behaviors
Major depressive disorder
Prolonged low mood and loss of interest impairing functioning
Bipolar disorder
Alternating episodes of depression and mania
Schizophrenia
Disorder with disorganized thinking, delusions, and hallucinations
Cognitive behavioral therapy
Treatment changing unhelpful thought patterns and behaviors
Psychoanalysis
Therapy exploring unconscious conflicts through free association
Systematic desensitization
Exposure therapy pairing relaxation with gradually feared stimuli
Social Psychology: Social psychology
Study of how people influence and relate to one another
Attribution theory
Explaining behavior as caused by the situation or the person
Fundamental attribution error
Overestimating personality and underestimating situation in others
Cognitive dissonance
Discomfort from holding conflicting beliefs, motivating attitude change
Conformity
Adjusting behavior to match group standards
Obedience
Following the commands of an authority figure
Groupthink
Poor decisions caused by a group's desire for harmony
Social facilitation
Improved performance on simple tasks when others are present
Social loafing
Reduced individual effort when working in a group
Deindividuation
Loss of self-awareness and restraint in group situations
Bystander effect
Reduced likelihood of helping when other people are present
In-group bias
Favoring one's own group over outsiders
Stereotype
A generalized belief about a group of people
Prejudice
An unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members
